en: ROGER MARTIN: This thing called planning has been around for a long, long time.
zh: 羅傑馬丁：規劃這種東西已經存在很久很久了。

en: People would plan out the activities they're going to engage in.
zh: 人們會計劃自己要參與的活動。

en: More recently, has been a discipline called strategy.
zh: 近年來，戰略這門學科應運而生。

en: People have put those two things together to call something strategic planning.
zh: 人們將這兩者結合起來，稱之為策略規劃。

notes.zh: come together：順利成形、水到渠成
notes.example: Everything came together right before the deadline.

en: Unfortunately, those things are not the same, strategy and planning.
zh: 遺憾的是，戰略和計劃並非同一回事。

en: So just putting them together and calling it strategic planning doesn't help.
zh: 和計劃並非同一回事。所以，光是把它們放在一起就稱之為策略規劃，是無濟於事的。商業領域中

notes.zh: come together：順利成形、水到渠成

en: What most strategic planning is in the world of business has nothing to do with strategy.
zh: 大多數策略規劃與策略本身毫無關係。

en: It's got the word, but it's not.
zh: 它有這個詞，但它不是。

en: It's a set of activities that the company says it's going to do.
zh: 這是該公司宣布將要進行的一系列活動。

en: We're going to improve customer experience.
zh: 我們將改善客戶體驗。

en: We're going to open this new plant.
zh: 我們將開設這家新工廠。

en: We're going to start a new talent development program.
zh: 我們將啟動一項新的人才培育計畫。列出了

en: A whole list of them, and they all sound good, but the results of all of those are not
zh: 一長串方案，每個方案聽起來都不錯，但所有這些方案的結果都不會讓

en: going to make the company happy because they didn't have a strategy.
zh: 公司滿意，因為他們沒有製定策略。

en: [MUSIC PLAYING] So what's a strategy?
zh: [音樂播放] 那麼，什麼是策略？

en: A strategy is an integrative set of choices that positions you on a playing field of your choice in a way
zh: 策略是一系列綜合性的選擇，它能讓你以自己選擇的方式在競爭環境中取得

en: that you win. So there's a theory.
zh: 勝利。所以，這是一種理論。

en: Strategy has a theory.
zh: 戰略是有理論的。

en: Here's why we should be on this playing field, not this other one, and here's how, on that playing field,
zh: 這就是為什麼我們應該在這個領域而不是另一個領域競爭，以及在這個領域，

en: we're going to be better than anybody else at serving the customers on that playing field.
zh: 我們如何比任何人都更好地服務這裡的客戶。

notes.zh: have better things to do：有更要緊的事要做
notes.example: I didn't want to bother you—you have better things to do.

notes.zh: Can I get you anything else?：餐廳服務生標準詢問句
notes.example: Can I get you anything else, like water?

en: That theory has to be coherent.
zh: 這個理論必須前後一致。

en: It has to be doable.
zh: 必須是可行的。

en: You have to be able to translate that into actions for it to be a great strategy.
zh: 要成為好的策略，就必須將策略轉化為行動。

en: Planning does not have to have any such coherence, and it typically is what people in manufacturing want--
zh: 計劃不必具有任何連貫性，它通常取決於製造業人員的意願——

en: the few things they want, to build a new plant, and the marketing people want to launch a new brand,
zh: 他們想要的幾件事，例如建造一座新工廠，行銷人員想要推出一個新品牌，

en: and the talent people want to hire more people-- that tends to be a list that has no internal coherence to it
zh: 人才管理人員想要招募更多的人—— 這往往是一份缺乏內部連貫性的清單，

en: and no specification of a way that that is going to accomplish collectively
zh: 也沒有具體說明如何共同

en: some goal for the company.
zh: 為公司實現某個目標。

en: See, planning is quite comforting.
zh: 你看，做好計劃會讓人感到很安心。

en: Plans typically have to do with the resources you're going to spend.
zh: 計劃通常與你將要投入的資源有關。

en: So we're going to build a plan.
zh: 所以我們要訂定一個計劃。

en: We're going to hire some people.
zh: 我們打算招一些人。

en: We're going to launch a new product.
zh: 我們將推出一款新產品。

en: Those are all things that are on the cost side of businesses.
zh: 這些都是企業營運成本的一部分。

en: Who controls your costs?
zh: 誰負責控制你的成本？

en: Who's the customer of your costs?
zh: 你的成本最終由誰承擔？

en: The answer is, you are.
zh: 答案是，你就是。

en: You decide how many square feet to lease, how many raw materials to buy, how many people to hire.
zh: 您可以自行決定租賃多少平方英尺的場地、購買多少原料、僱用多少員工。

en: Those are more comfortable because you control them.
zh: 這些更舒適，因為你可以控制它們。

notes.zh: keep control over...：掌控某人或某事
notes.example: Staying calm helps you keep control over the conversation.

en: A strategy, on the other hand, specifies an outcome, a competitive outcome that you wish to achieve,
zh: 另一方面，策略則規定了你希望實現的競爭結果，即

en: which involves customers wanting your product or service
zh: 客戶對你的產品或服務有

en: enough that they will buy enough of it to make the profitability that you'd like to make.
zh: 足夠的需求，以至於他們會購買足夠的量，從而獲得你想要獲得的利潤。

en: The tricky thing about that is that you don't control them.
zh: 棘手之處在於你無法控制他們。

notes.zh: keep control over...：掌控某人或某事
notes.example: Staying calm helps you keep control over the conversation.

en: You might wish you could, but you can't.
zh: 你或許希望自己能做到，但你做不到。

en: They decide, not you. That's a harder trick.
zh: 他們做決定，不是你。那可就難多了。

en: So that means putting yourself out and saying, here's what we believe will happen.
zh: 所以這意味著你要站出來，說：我們認為會發生這樣的事情。

en: We can't prove it in advance, we can't guarantee it, but this is what we want to have happen
zh: 我們無法提前證明，也無法保證，但這正是我們希望發生

en: and that we believe will happen.
zh: 並相信會發生的事。

en: It's much easier to say, I'll build a factory, I will hire more people, et cetera,
zh: 說「 我要建造一家工廠，我要僱用更多的人」等等

en: than I will have customers end up liking our offering more
zh: 要比讓客戶最終更喜歡我們的產品而

en: than those of competitors.
zh: 不是競爭對手的產品容易得多。

en: The tricky thing about planning is that while you're planning,
zh: 計劃的棘手之處在於，當你制定計劃時，很

en: chances are at least one competitor is figuring out how to win.
zh: 可能至少有一個競爭對手正在思考如何取勝。

en: When US air carriers were busily planning what routes to fly
zh: 當美國各航空公司忙著規劃航線

en: and da-da-da, there was this little company
zh: 等等的時候，德州有一家名為西南航空的小公司，卻制定了

en: in Texas called Southwest that had a strategy for winning.
zh: 致勝策略。

en: And at first, that looked largely irrelevant because it was tiny.
zh: 起初，這看起來無關緊要，因為它很小。

en: What Southwest Airlines was aiming for was an outcome.
zh: 西南航空的目標是取得某種結果。

en: What they wanted to be is a substitute for Greyhound, a way more convenient way
zh: 他們想要成為灰狗巴士的替代品，一種更方便的

en: to get around at a price that wasn't extraordinarily much greater than a Greyhound bus.
zh: 出行方式，而且價格不會比灰狗巴士貴太多。

en: Southwest said, everybody else is flying hub and spoke.
zh: 西南航空表示，其他航空公司都是採用樞紐輻射式航線。

notes.zh: Can I get you anything else?：餐廳服務生標準詢問句

en: They have hubs, and they fly hub and spoke.
zh: 他們有樞紐，他們採用樞紐輻射式航線。

en: We're going to fly point to point so that we don't have aircraft waiting on the ground because you only make money
zh: 我們將採用點對點飛行方式，這樣就不會有飛機在地面等待，因為只有

en: when you're in the air.
zh: 在空中才能賺錢。

en: We're going to only fly 737s, one kind of aircraft, so that our gates are set up for those,
zh: 我們將只運作 737 機型，一種飛機，所以我們的登機口是為這種飛機設定的，

en: our systems are set up for those, our training, our simulations are set up.
zh: 我們的系統是為這種飛機設定的，我們的訓練和模擬也是為這種飛機設定的。

en: We're not going to offer meals on the flights because we're going to specialize in short flights.
zh: 我們將不提供航班餐食，因為我們將專注於短程航班。

en: We're not going to book through travel agents.
zh: 我們不會透過旅行社預訂。

en: We're going to encourage people to book online because that's less expensive for everybody and more convenient.
zh: 我們將鼓勵大家在線上預訂，因為這樣對每個人來說都更便宜、更方便。

en: So their strategy ended up having a substantially lower cost than any of the major carriers so
zh: 因此，他們的策略最終成本遠低於任何一家主要航空公司，

en: that they could offer substantially lower prices.
zh: 從而能夠提供更低的價格。

en: Because it had a way of winning, it got bigger and then bigger and then bigger and then bigger
zh: 因為它有取勝之道，所以它越做越大，越做越大，越做越大，最終成為

en: and bigger and bigger and bigger until it flies the most passenger seat miles in America.
zh: 美國客運里程最長的航空公司。

en: The major carriers were not trying to win against one another.
zh: 各大航空公司之間並沒有相互競爭。

en: They were all playing to play, as I say.
zh: 正如我所說，他們都只是為了比賽而比賽。

en: They were playing to participate, maybe buy more planes, get more gates, maybe grow some,

zh: 做舒適但對你無益的事情的舒適陷阱，你該如何開始呢？

en: The most important thing to recognize is that strategy will have angst associated with it.
zh: 最重要的是要認識到，制定策略必然會伴隨著焦慮。

en: It'll make you feel somewhat nervous because as a manager, chances are you've been taught you should do things
zh: 這會讓你感到有些緊張，因為身為管理者，你很可能被教導要做一些

en: that you can prove in advance.
zh: 可以事先證明的事情。

en: You can't prove in advance that your strategy will succeed.
zh: 你無法事先證明你的策略一定會成功。

en: You can look at a plan and say, well, all of these things are doable.
zh: 你可以看看計劃，然後說，嗯，所有這些事情都是可以實現的。

en: Let's just do those because they're within our control.
zh: 我們就做這些事吧，因為它們在我們掌控之中。

en: But they won't add up to much.
zh: 但它們加起來也

en: to work? Why do you do that?

zh: （對照上方英文字幕跟讀）
